albiglutide.text: Albiglutide is a withdrawn weekly GLP-1 diabetes drug that fat-loss readers sometimes cite as an early member of the GLP-1 family behind newer weight-loss injections. Its weight effects in diabetes trials were modest, and it was never studied as an appearance or cutting tool.

peptide-yy.text: Peptide YY is a gut hormone released after meals, and users interested in appetite control discuss it as a natural fullness signal that could support dieting toward a leaner physique. Infusion studies show reduced food intake; use for appearance is untested and it is not an established tool.

ace-031.text: ACE-031 is an experimental myostatin-blocking protein that muscle-focused forum users cite as a route to growth beyond natural limits. It was tested in healthy women and boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy, where it raised muscle measures; physique use in healthy lifters is untested and the trials ended.

stamulumab.text: Stamulumab is a discontinued antibody against myostatin that muscle-minded readers mention as an early attempt at removing the body's growth brake. It was tested in muscular dystrophy rather than for physique, so appearance use in healthy people is untested.

aro-inhbe.text: ARO-INHBE is an experimental RNAi drug that fat-loss followers watch because it targets fat distribution rather than appetite, with the hope of a leaner waistline. It is in early obesity trials only; its effect on appearance is untested and no results are available.

chain: Fat cells release more stored fat
aro-alk7.text: ARO-ALK7 is an experimental RNAi drug aimed at a fat-cell signalling receptor, discussed by fat-loss followers as a possible non-appetite route to losing body fat. A single early obesity trial is recruiting; appearance outcomes are untested.

chain: Fat cells break down more fat
wve-007.text: WVE-007 is an experimental siRNA that body-composition enthusiasts follow because its stated goal is losing visceral fat while preserving lean mass. Evidence so far is early company data; its effect on appearance has not been studied in published trials.

aln-6222.text: ALN-6222 is an experimental RNAi drug aimed at INHBE, a gene tied to fat distribution, and is followed by fat-loss readers as a possible next-generation obesity therapy. It has only just entered its first trial, so its appearance effects are untested.

monlunabant.text: Monlunabant is an experimental oral CB1 blocker that fat-loss followers watch as a possible pill alternative to GLP-1 injections. Phase 2 showed modest weight loss with some neuropsychiatric side effects; its use for appearance beyond obesity treatment is untested.

crb-913.text: CRB-913 is an experimental CB1 blocker followed by fat-loss readers as a possible add-on to GLP-1 drugs. It boosted weight loss in obese mice; human data are not yet public, so appearance use is untested.

nimacimab.text: Nimacimab is an experimental anti-CB1 antibody that fat-loss followers track as a peripherally acting obesity drug. It is in Phase 2 for obesity; any use for appearance is untested.

nad-injections.text: Injected NAD+ is promoted by longevity clinics and online communities as an anti-aging and energy treatment, with users hoping for fresher skin and a more youthful look. The appearance claim rests on cell biology and anecdote; controlled human trials for aging or looks are lacking.

glutathione-injections.text: Injected glutathione, often paired with vitamin C, is used in some countries and online communities to lighten skin and even out tone. Evidence for skin lightening comes from small studies of mixed quality; its effectiveness is unclear.

vip-vasoactive-intestinal-peptide.text: VIP is a natural vasodilating neuropeptide sold as a research peptide, and users speculate it could aid recovery and circulation. No human studies address any appearance use; its established research concerns gut, lung and immune function.

chain: Used for erectile function and lung disease
aviptadil.text: Aviptadil is synthetic VIP used with phentolamine as an injection for erectile dysfunction in some European countries and tested in COVID-19 lung failure. Peptide communities mention it alongside VIP for circulation and recovery; no appearance use has been studied.

ara-290.text: ARA 290 is an EPO-derived repair peptide that recovery-focused users discuss for tissue protection and nerve healing. It has been tested in small neuropathy trials; use for recovery or appearance in healthy people is untested.

b7-33.text: B7-33 is a lab-made relaxin mimic studied in animals for fibrosis, and peptide communities speculate about it for tissue repair and scar reduction. There are no human trials and no documented appearance use.

pe-22-28.text: PE-22-28 is a spadin-derived peptide researched in rodents as a fast-acting antidepressant, and some peptide users discuss it for mood and mental sharpness. Human data are absent and no direct appearance use is documented.

pnc-27.text: PNC-27 is a p53-derived peptide that kills cancer cells in laboratory studies and is sold as a research chemical, with longevity-minded users interested in it. No human trials exist and no appearance use is documented.

erythropoietin.text: Erythropoietin is a kidney hormone and anaemia drug used for endurance doping, and some physique users discuss it for stamina and recovery capacity in training. Its performance effects are studied in endurance athletes; a direct effect on muscle or appearance is untested.

abaloparatide.text: Abaloparatide is an approved osteoporosis bone-builder that forum users speculate about alongside bonesmashing, orthodontics and limb lengthening for facial structure and height. It has been studied for fracture risk in osteoporosis; no trials address facial bone or appearance.

salmon-calcitonin.text: Salmon calcitonin is used for Paget's disease and high blood calcium, and bone-focused readers mention it as a way to slow bone loss. It has no documented appearance use and is not studied for facial structure.

osteocalcin.text: Osteocalcin is a bone-made protein and proposed hormone, and bone-focused readers connect it to bone strength and metabolism. It is studied as a marker of bone formation and for metabolic effects; no looks-related use has been tested in humans.

irisin.text: Irisin is a proposed exercise hormone that fat-loss readers cite as a way exercise might brown fat and raise energy expenditure. The browning finding comes from mice; human evidence is thin and disputed.

adropin.text: Adropin is a liver and brain peptide linked in mice to fat and glucose metabolism, and fat-loss readers discuss it as a possible metabolic lever. Human data are blood-level associations only; appearance use is untested.

chain: Blocking it might ease weight gain
asprosin.text: Asprosin is a fat-derived fasting hormone that raises glucose and appetite in mice, and fat-loss readers follow it as a possible appetite target. High levels track with obesity; no appearance use exists.

obestatin.text: Obestatin is a ghrelin-gene peptide first reported to curb appetite, which led fat-loss readers to see it as a possible diet aid. Both its appetite effect and its receptor remain disputed, and appearance use is untested.

limostatin.text: Limostatin is a fruit-fly hormone that suppresses insulin during fasting, and metabolism-minded readers cite it as a model for how fasting signals fat handling. It has been studied only in insects, with no human data.

alamandine.text: Alamandine is a blood-pressure-regulating peptide of the renin-angiotensin system, discussed by longevity-minded readers for cardiovascular and tissue-protective effects. It has been studied in rodents; no human trials or appearance use exist.

thyrotropin-releasing-hormone.text: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone sits at the top of the thyroid axis, and hormone-minded readers discuss it for thyroid, mood and energy effects. Human studies outside diagnostics are small and dated; appearance use is untested.
